## Libraries and data load

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(glmnet)
library(ranger)
library(tidyclust)
library(cluster)
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
final_raw <- read_csv("data/gapminder_final_F26.csv")
```

We study GDP per person (`gdp`) as the regression response and the four-category
world region (`world_4region`) as the classification response. We use the
remaining measurements as candidate predictors, apart from identifiers and
the exclusions explained below.

## Exploratory data analysis (EDA) part 1

### Checking for missing data

```{r}
countries <- final_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(population)) |>
  mutate(across(c(world_4region, landlocked, democracy, female_hos,
                  freedom_status, income_level, sexual_harassment), as.factor))
countries
```

The file has 273 geographic records, but 79 lack population and nearly all
other substantive measurements including territories and historical
entities. So we restrict the analysis to the 194 countries with population
data.

```{r}
missing_data <- final_raw |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Raw_missing") |>
  left_join(countries |>
    summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable",
                 values_to = "Country_missing"), by = "Variable") |>
  arrange(desc(Country_missing))
missing_data
```

Disregarding those 79 countries that have no records, energy use has 153 missing
values, and disaster deaths have 94. These are the clearest candidates for
removal before modeling.

### Units of variables

```{r}
variable_dictionary <- read_excel("data/Gapminder_Var_Dict_F26.xlsx") |>
  # Match variable names with the data we have
  mutate(Variable = recode(Variable, cell_phone = "cell_phones",
    corruption = "corruption_index", education = "education_index",
    electriciy_access = "electricity_access", sanitation_pct = "basic_sanitation"))
variable_dictionary
```

The table gives the supplied definitions and measurement years. GDP, CO2,
health spending, and alcohol are already per person; cell phones are per 100
people. Child mortality is per 1,000 live births, maternal mortality per 100,000
live births, and the murder, traffic, and suicide rates per 100,000 people.
Natural-disaster deaths are a total count, so we convert them to deaths per
100,000 residents.

```{r}
countries <- countries |>
  mutate(natural_disaster_rate = 100000 * natural_disaster_deaths / population)
```

### Logging variables

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 24
countries |>
  # Exclude categorical variables
  select(-c(geo, name, world_4region, landlocked, democracy, female_hos,
            freedom_status, income_level, sexual_harassment)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Value)) + geom_histogram(bins = 20) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Original value", y = "Countries")
```

We use log10 transformations for those variables that have long upper tails.
This reduces the influence of very large values and gives more space to
differences among lower values.

```{r}
log_variables <- c("cell_phones", "child_mortality", "co2_per_capita", 
  "daily_income", "gdp", "health_spending_per_person", "maternal_mortality",
  "murder_rate", "natural_disaster_rate", "population", "poverty_rate",
  "traffic_deaths")
final_logged <- countries |>
  mutate(across(all_of(log_variables), log10))
```

```{r}
final_logged |>
  select(gdp, population, daily_income, co2_per_capita, child_mortality,
         health_spending_per_person, maternal_mortality, natural_disaster_rate) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Value)) + geom_histogram(bins = 20) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "log10 value", y = "Countries")
```

## CV or testing/training for overfitting

```{r}
model_data <- final_logged |>
  select(-geo, -name, -energy_use_per_person, -natural_disaster_rate)
set.seed(2026)
final_split <- initial_split(model_data, prop = 0.8, strata = world_4region)
final_train <- training(final_split)
final_test <- testing(final_split)
tibble(Set = c("Training", "Testing"), Countries = c(nrow(final_train), nrow(final_test)))
```

We reserve about 20% of countries for testing and stratify by region to keep
all four regions represented. Country name, country code, and the two columns
above 40% missing are now excluded.
We plan to use 5 fold CV within training to choose tuning parameters.
